hints: The block is at rest. Is friction then at its limit, or only as large as needed?
worded:
1. The block is at rest, so friction is static and self-adjusting: it equals whatever balances the horizontal forces.

2. The only other horizontal force is F cos θ, so friction = F cos θ, opposite to it. (A)

3. (B) is the limiting value for this push (N = mg + F sin θ); friction reaches it only on the verge of slipping. (C) would be the limit for a pull, (D) for no vertical push.
conventional:
![](asset:P000541-sol-1)

At rest: $\sum F_{x} = 0\mkern6mu  \Rightarrow \mkern6mu  f = F\cos\theta$ (static, $\leq \mu\left( Mg + F\sin\theta \right)$).
mistakes: Do not write μN for a body at rest unless it is on the verge of slipping.
